subject: english-literature
title: Temporal Structures
welcome_lead: How texts handle time — flashback, foreshadowing, in medias res — is central to Time & Space. Narrative order is rarely chronological.
meta_desc: English Literature: temporal structure, flashback, foreshadowing, narrative order.
final_note: Time in fiction bends — and the bending carries meaning.

concepts.def: Genette's term for flashback — a return to an earlier event.
Genette's term for flash-forward or foreshadowing.
Beginning a narrative in the middle of the action.
Story is the chronological events; discourse is the order in which they are told.
The relation between the time events take in the story and the space they occupy in the text.
How often an event is narrated relative to how often it occurs.

walkthroughs.body_html: A flashback (analepsis) recovers past time; a flash-forward (prolepsis) anticipates the future. Toni Morrison's Beloved uses analepsis to make the past inescapable.
The chronological events constitute the fabula (story); the order of telling is the sjuzhet (discourse). A detective novel often reverses chronology — the murder is told last.
A single moment may fill twenty pages (Joyce's epiphanies); years may pass in a sentence. The compression or expansion signals importance.
